beats.n: The Watch takes Pell down the back stair, by his own request, so that the guests will not see him. He walks with his hands in front of him, like a man carrying something that might spill.
Master Vennard's death is entered as murder, and his killer is named. Miss Odalys asks, very quietly, whether the fire of 1166 might be looked at again. It is a request, not an accusation.
You say you will see what the Hall of Records holds.
You keep the whistle in a drawer at the Watch House. Sometimes, on wet nights, you take it out.
The Chief Constable reads your report twice, and reads the word apoplexy once more, aloud, with evident pleasure.

beats.t: "Quite right, Hale. A great man, a great strain. Sensible of you."

beats.n: Master Vennard is buried with speeches. The Memorial Lamp is unveiled a week late, and its plaque is very well engraved.
The wall bracket is repainted. The tin, the wrench, and the little brass whistle stay where they are, waiting for someone to look.
